Yes, the story has an appropriate balance between scene and summary/exposition. 

The narrative primarily unfolds as a real-time scene on the boat, using vivid sensory details (the smell of diesel, the sound of the flag and water, the rain) and sparse, realistic dialogue to build quiet tension between Ilse and Jonas. At the same time, the author seamlessly weaves in brief moments of exposition and summary—such as the memory of Jonas freezing as a child and Henning putting a hat on him, the progression of the stiffness in Ilse's knuckles since autumn, and the detail about stripping the guest room bed two weeks ago. These brief summaries enrich the scene with character history and emotional subtext without interrupting the pacing of the present interaction.
